newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Kumagai hopes to list unit in mid-1997.
newsitem.headline: Kumagai hopes to list unit in mid-1997.

text.p: Kumagai Gumi (Hong Kong) Ltd hopes to list its infrastructure unit in the Yangpu industrial zone of southern China in mid-1997, its deputy chairman said in an interview.

"Our hope is to get it done before the middle of this year...before the July 1 handover date. I think it would be interesting to float the Yangpu concept before that," Frederick Ma, deputy chairman of Kumagai Gumi, told Reuters.
Hong Kong will hand over to Chinese rule on July 1.
Ma said it was very difficult to pinpoint the exact date of the listing because the timing was dictated by many factors including market sentiment. The size of the issue was not fixed yet, he added.
Kumagai Gumi announced the planned spin-off of its infrastructure project in the Yangpu industrial zone, in Hainan province, in early 1996.
"We would like to see the deal floated during the time when we can secure a few very eye catching deals," Ma said.
Last week, Kumagai Gumi said China National Offshore Oil Corp had agreed to take part in a 15.58 billion yuan fertiliser project in the Yangpu Economic Development Zone.

Apart from the fertiliser project, Ma said "we are working on a couple of other deals including a pulp and paper factory, supply of natural gas...glass, steel plant...We have a few big deals centering on foreign investors."
